use: Templates show layout, composition, hierarchy and rhythm only. Never copy their text, numbers, claims, client names or logos: content comes from the user. Their colours, fonts and sizes need not match the design system; build every output with design-system tokens, text roles, components and assets. Pick the template whose structure fits the user's content, then adapt it.
source: Figma Design MCP, the Template frame on the outcome's page

sections.name: Design-language references
sections.use: Architecture references for the overall design language: how devices, zones, connections and the platform are drawn.

templates.name: Machine monitoring · sensors to platform
templates.layout: Machines in a left column (icon and label); a sensor beside each; dashed connectors to Wi-Fi routers, then 4G uplinks to the platform panel on the right: a dashed-outline panel with the platform logo tile, a stack of feature buttons and a row of small capability tiles.

templates.name: Process diagram · heat exchanger
templates.layout: The process drawn as a line diagram (pipes, heat exchanger, steam trap, valves) with sensors placed on it and short labels; wireless links to a LoRa gateway, then cloud, then the platform panel on the right with feature buttons and dashboard screenshots; DCS and industrial PC boxes along the top.

templates.name: Repeated units · steam traps
templates.layout: Three identical device rows (steam trap with its node) on the left, labelled once with 'up to N per gateway'; wireless links to a central gateway; cloud, then the platform panel on the right; a small box of key process parameters.

templates.name: Cloud architecture · substations
templates.layout: Title top-left with the logo top-right; three stacked zones (one per substation), each a grid of energy meters feeding gateways; network links to a cloud node, then the platform panel on the right with screenshots.

templates.name: Camera-based vision system
templates.layout: The physical process on the left as a 3D scene (conveyor with cameras and lights placed where they sit); tinted zones with a header tag (junction box, control room, IT network), devices as image plus name tag inside them; labelled links (OFC, Ethernet) between zones; end devices top-right; the platform as one large panel bottom-right with its outputs as a branched list of buttons and dashboard screenshots.
